content.text: {"conditions":{"rc1":{"status":"review","note":"Most agency findings tie back to ROI-cited evidence (IPO's use of 'mothering', the Feb 24-25 steps, the May 2020 tasks), but the record has gaps in the path to the conclusion, such as the FAD's reliance on mediation 'changes' and a written apology that Complainant says never occurred, and it never reconciles the workload dispute (IPO's time estimates vs. Complainant's 'unprecedented' claim)."},"rc2":{"status":"review","note":"Most characterizations carry ROI page citations and are attributed to Complainant, the IPO, HR-1 or Subordinate-1, but several FAD findings (no other demeaning language, mediation outcomes, IPO unaware of performance change) lack clear sources, and the HR-1 call is undated and unsupported by any corroboration."},"rc3":{"status":"pass","note":"Dated events are traceable in order (Oct 2019 complaints, Jan 31 counseling, Feb 24-25 memo and meeting, March 2020 follow-up, May 13-15 tasking, June 15 transfer, May 31 complaint, June 3, 2021 FAD), though the HR-1 phone call is undated."},"rc4":{"status":"gap","note":"The FAD does not identify who prepared the analysis, and it did not address the omissions Complainant raised in her April 19, 2021 letter (uninterviewed Subordinate-2, Subordinate-3, HR-2), so the record does not show that responsive information was considered before finalization."},"rc5":{"status":"gap","note":"Key witnesses (Subordinate-2, Subordinate-3, HR-2) were never interviewed, the FAD contains disputed or unsupported statements (written apology, mediation changes), and the Agency filed no response on appeal, so an independent reviewer could not assess whether the conclusion is supported without outside context."}}}
